title: Release Train Telescope & Week-of-Go-Live Synchronizer
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem statement: As we scale concurrent launches across runtime, console, and API, the current calendar view and manual week-of-go-live coordination create last-minute capacity conflicts and communications fatigue for oncall and launch owners. Teams reserve 'soft' capacity but there is no central mechanism to convert those reservations into enforceable stability credits or to synthesize a single-week harmonized schedule across release trains.

Goal: Build a small orchestration layer and runbook called the 'Telescope' that provides a 6-week forward view of release conflicts, allocates stability credits for critical weeks, and drives an automated week-of-go-live synchronizer that produces a fixed cutover slate, guardrails, and an oncall riser roster. The deliverable is a lightweight product+ops flow (UI + runbook + Slack-based signals) for Q4 launches and a pilot with 3 teams (runtime, console, api).

Scope:
- Read-only Telescope view that aggregates planned release slots from each train and flags overlaps and overcommitted critical-path services.
- Stability credit allocator: a policy engine that assigns up to N credits per week by priority, with a manual override UI for PMs and EMs.
- Week-of-Go-Live synchronizer: a small workflow that, 7 days and 24 hours before cutover, posts a harmonized checklist to the launch channel, triggers a capacity-hedge ticket if concurrency > threshold, and produces an oncall escalation map.
- Integration points: release Calendar (source of truth), Console capacity dashboard, Dedicated capacity reservation API, and Canary scheduling service.

Out of scope: automatic deployment gating, long-term ML-based conflict prediction (phase 2).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Why now: Rising frequency of simultaneous train activity and inability to proactively reserve capacity has led to three week-of-go-live collisions in the last quarter, each requiring manual rollbacks or emergency capacity purchases. A small centralized tool and runbook will reduce churn and improve stabilty for customer-facing launches.
acceptance_criteria: Telescope UI shows aggregated 6-week horizon with conflict highlighting for runtime/console/api trains
Stability credit allocator runs a deterministic policy and exposes manual override; logs stored to release ledger
Week-of-Go-Live synchronizer posts the harmonized checklist at T-7d and T-24h to the launch Slack channel
Pilot executed with runtime, console, and api teams for two launches with post-launch metrics captured
No regressions in release pipeline and at least 30% reduction in last-minute capacity escalations for pilot launches
